Right-angle marks are visible at the upper-right corner and the lower-left corner. A dashed diagonal connects the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner, and near the lower-right corner it is labeled 62°; this angle is between the dashed diagonal and the right vertical side. Reasoning: Let the vertical side length be h and the horizontal side length be 3. In the right triangle formed by the upper-left corner, upper-right corner, and lower-right corner, relative to the 62° at the lower-right corner, the upper horizontal side 3 is the opposite side, and the right vertical side h is the adjacent side, so tan(62°)=3/h. method.method_draft: Read the figure as a rectangle: the horizontal top/bottom side is labeled 3 in., the vertical sides are equal, and a dashed diagonal runs from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner. With respect to the 62° angle, the opposite leg is the horizontal length 3 and the adjacent leg is the rectangle height h, so tan(62°) = 3/h. Solve h = 3/tan(62°), then compute perimeter P = 2(3 + h) and round.
